peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NATGAS 45.7% with 3/3 replicate support; SP500 19.6% with 2/3 replicate support; XYZ100 19.6% with 2/3 replicate support; TSLA 15.2% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: Natural gas
peers.reason: Natural gas is the key fuel input for Bloom Energy's solid oxide fuel cell servers, so gas price and availability directly affect deployment economics and margins. This shared input-cost exposure gets the largest peer weight; NATGAS shows 4.546 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity.

peers.name: S&P 500
peers.reason: The primary hedge is also one of the closest return comparators, since a large share of BE's daily return variance is simply broad U.S. equity market movement. Including it in the basket at a substantial weight correctly reflects that systematic exposure instead of forcing the weight into remote factor analogies, and its 89.219 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity makes it the most liquid instrument in the basket.

peers.name: Nasdaq-100
peers.reason: Nasdaq-100 captures the AI and data-center capital-spending cycle that drives demand for Bloom's onsite power, along with growth-stock duration. It is used as a dominant sector and systematic comparator, not as a generic high-beta analogy, and shows 112.11 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Tesla is the closest single-name economic analog available: a vertically integrated clean-energy technology hardware company whose valuation is driven by energy generation and storage deployment economics, policy-sensitive clean-tech demand, and the same growth-equity investor base as BE. It is a sector-adjacent substitute exposure rather than a mere high-beta analogy, and its 24-hour perp liquidity of 8.958 USD millions exceeds BE's 5.895 USD millions.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: Bloom Energy is a U.S.-listed mid-cap growth equity whose dominant generic systematic driver is the broad U.S. equity market. The S&P 500 is the cleanest, most liquid broad equity index in the universe, with 24-hour perp liquidity of 89.219 USD millions versus BE's own 5.895 USD millions, making it the natural instrument to absorb generic market beta so the peer basket can isolate BE-specific economics. The Nasdaq-100 was considered but rejected because BE is NYSE-listed and is not a Nasdaq-100 constituent, so the S&P 500 is the more defensible systematic hedge.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
